title: Learned causal GRU box refiner, version 2 (offline: data, training, evaluation) - pre-registration
written: 2026-11-15 21:12 (PC clock; file time stamp), before any v2 model was trained and before any v2 number on val-A or val-B. Code written so far: gru_v2/scripts/g2_lib.py, g2_data.py, g2_train.py; only a 4-sequence smoke run of the training-piece builder on TRAIN sequences was done (no metric).
what_was_already_seen: val-B (TMOT val seq2, 17, 22, 47, 54, 66 + DanceTrack 0012, 0033, 0055, 0075, 0087, 0096, 0098, 0099) is NOT a fresh test set. It was reported in round 1 (results/ref_valB.json), in the independent verification (verify/checkB_*.json, verify/combo/combo_valB.json) and in the size-mode workflow (v2/results/size_valB.json). I read those numbers (REVIEW_FINDINGS_20261115.json) and they shaped this design (start transient, lag against the detection, conv_euro baseline). For v2 it is used ONCE, after every choice below is fixed on train / val-A.
user_decision: GRU route for a continuously, naturally changing person box; fix the GRU now against the current detectors (near = 11-14 body-box pose model expE_v1_best, far / general = farc2 C_control_v1_epoch2), no wait for the detector retrain.

data.splits: PREREG_POS_REFINE_20261115 splits unchanged: train = TMOT 19 + DanceTrack 28; val-A = TMOT seq12, 18, 26, 48, 64 + DanceTrack 0023, 0045, 0066, 0086; val-B as above.
data.inputs_reused: round-1 files, read only: data/det (detections of both detectors), data/assoc (GT association and head-to-hip targets), data/gmc (camera warps), data/tracks (server-like ByteTrack rows, streams near / far / sw). No detection is rerun.
data.target: the round-1 head-to-hip body box target (tgt_h2h), unchanged.
data.lookup: data/lut_train.pkl = a copy of verify/lut.pkl (the verifier's train-split table: detector box height x aspect bin -> median target / detector relation). Baselines 'conv' and 'conv_euro' use it with hard bins exactly as the verifier did. The v2 model uses the same table read with bilinear interpolation between bin centres (first / last height centre 20 / 280 px, first / last aspect centre 0.27 / 0.90) as its base box; no new fit.
data.training_pieces: per GT person of the train split: near / far / spliced near<->far (ref_lib.splice), synthetic occluder (ref_lib.occlude), left-right flip p 0.5, NEW frame-rate change per sequence version: p 0.15 every other frame (half rate), p 0.30 doubled rate (a synthetic frame between two real ones: mean box + fresh noise of the track's own frame-to-frame noise size, mean keypoints, mean target, half camera warp), NEW random track start p 0.5 (the first rows dropped), pieces of at most 256 rows, each piece a fresh state (so every piece start is a track start). 6 versions, one per epoch.

model.engine: one frame-by-frame engine, batch over the people of the frame, used for training data, validation, the device-rate test and the cost test (g2_lib.Engine). Per id: previous detection box and previous output kept in the current frame's coordinates (moved by every frame's camera warp), fixed-gain velocity filter (gain 0.35; replaces the round-1 per-person Kalman so everything is one array operation), frames missed, rows since the state started. State reset: more than 30 frames missed, or detection centre farther than 1.5 previous-box heights from the camera-moved previous detection.
model.inputs: 78 per person and frame: velocity 2, innovation 2, centre change 2, log size change 2, log h / 100, log w / h, picture edges 4, keypoints 51, frames missed, camera shift 2, lookup correction 4, start flag, rows since start, and (arch gate) the previous output relative to the converted box 4.
model.output: arch 'gate': box = previous output (camera-moved) + g x (converted box - previous output) + correction, g in (0,1) per component (cx, cy, log w, log h) from the GRU, correction within +-0.4 converted heights / size x/ 2.2; on the first row of a state: converted box + correction. arch 'res': converted box + correction (no feedback). GRUCell(78, 48) + Linear(48, 8), head zero-initialised (gate bias 1).
model.no_dt_input: the GRU sees per-frame quantities only (no seconds). Frame-rate robustness comes from the rate augmentation; the size filter after it works in seconds.
model.loss: acc (smooth-L1 beta 0.02 of the round-1 error vector against the target, rows 0-4 of a state weighted x3) + lam_j x own jitter (smooth-L1 of the camera-compensated second difference of the OUTPUT itself: centre / own height, log w, log h) + 2 x step hinge (relu(|d log h| - 0.04) + 0.5 relu(|d log w| - 0.06) per frame) + lam_l x (|mean lag| in the 0.03-0.1 bin + |mean lag| in the > 0.1 bin), lag = (output centre - converted detection centre) along the target motion / target height, mean over the batch chunk.
model.training: PC CPU, AdamW lr 2e-3 (the round-1 val-A choice) cosine to 2 %, weight decay 1e-4, 30 epochs, batch 64 pieces, truncated BPTT 64 rows, grad clip 1. Epoch inside a run: lowest value of the run's own loss on the val-A rows.

grids.gru: arch in {gate, res} x lam_j in {1, 4} x lam_l in {1, 4}: 8 runs.
grids.size_filter: after the chosen GRU: One Euro on log w / log h only (centre untouched, camera scale compensated, dt in seconds, reset with the GRU state): mc_s in {1.5, 3, 5} Hz x beta_s in {0, 0.3, 1}, dcut 1 Hz: 9 points (includes the verifier's combination a = 5 / 1).
grids.conv_euro_t: like-for-like tuned baseline: lookup (hard bins) + One Euro with centre mc in {0.4, 1, 3} x beta in {0.3, 1, 3} x mc_s in {0.4, 1.5, 5} x beta_s in {0, 0.3, 1}: 81 points, chosen with the SAME val-A rule as the GRU.

metrics: verify/combo definitions (per row against the head-to-hip target, in target heights): ce centre error (cap 2), aim = aim-point (top + 0.37 h) error, lh = |log h / h_target|, dh / da = one-frame height / aim-point change on consecutive frames, jitter = RMS second difference of the output itself (d2c centre, d2a aim point), per-track largest dh (median over tracks with >= 10 steps). NEW: first5 = rows 1-4 of a state (the steps inside the first 5 rows), for people with GT height under 100 px: mean dh, share of row-1 steps > 0.15, median height / target at rows 0, 1, 4. NEW lag against the CURRENT detection along the target motion, per target-speed bin (0-0.01, 0.01-0.03, 0.03-0.1, > 0.1 heights per frame): along_det = (output centre - detection centre) . u / target h, where the detection is taken in the method's own box definition (raw detection for raw / tracker / euro; lookup-converted detection (hard bins) for conv, conv_euro, gru_v1, gru_v2, gru_v2_size); along_raw = the same against the raw detection centre for every method (the verifier's definition), reported for >= 100 px. Negative = behind.
methods_reported: raw, tracker (Kalman row), euro (round-1 One Euro mc 3 beta 3 mc_s 0.4 beta_s 0.3 on the raw box), conv, conv_euro (lookup + the same One Euro, the verifier's baseline), conv_euro_t (tuned as above), gru_v1 (export/box_refine_gru_tmotdance_20261115.npz, ref_lib.run_ref), gru_v2, gru_v2_size. All except gru_v1 use the engine's state starts as the reset rule; gru_v1 keeps its own round-1 rule so its round-1 numbers reproduce.

selection_valA.rows: val-A, streams near + far + sw pooled, per dataset (TMOT, DanceTrack).
selection_valA.score: J = mean over the two datasets of the mean of four ratios against conv_euro on the same rows: dh p99, per-track largest dh (median), aim jitter (d2a RMS), first5 mean dh (people under 100 px). Lower is smoother.
selection_valA.gates: in BOTH datasets: (G1) aim error <= conv_euro aim error x 1.02 + 0.001; (G2) lag: along_det in the > 0.1 bin >= min(tracker, conv_euro) - 0.015 and in the 0.03-0.1 bin >= min(tracker, conv_euro) - 0.010; (G3) share of row-1 steps > 0.15 (people under 100 px) <= 0.10.
selection_valA.rule: among candidates passing all gates the lowest J; if none passes, the candidate with the smallest summed gate violation (in the gates' own units), and the report says so. The same rule picks conv_euro_t (its gate reference stays conv_euro).
selection_valA.size_filter_rule: on the chosen GRU: gates relative to gru_v2 alone in both datasets: |log h| error <= gru_v2 + 0.003, aim error <= gru_v2 + 0.001, size lag (signed log-h error along the target's height change, > 0.03 log per frame) >= gru_v2 - 0.015; among passing points the lowest mean ratio (dh p99, per-track largest dh) against gru_v2; if none passes, mc_s 5 / beta_s 1 (the verifier's a).

valB_once.rows: main tables: near + far streams pooled per dataset (as round 1 and the verification); the switch stream is reported separately and is not part of the pass rules.
valB_once.bootstrap: per-sequence bootstrap, 2000 draws, seed 0, 90 % intervals (ref_eval.boot_mean / boot_diff, combo_lib.boot_pct / boot_trackmax).
valB_once.candidates: gru_v2 and gru_v2_size are both judged; the proposed final form is gru_v2_size.

pass_rules.P1_smoother_than_tracker: in both datasets: dh p99, per-track largest dh (median) and aim jitter^2 all lower than the tracker row (point estimate), and the upper end of the 90 % interval of the difference below 0 for at least two of the three.
pass_rules.P2_smoother_than_conv_euro: the same three against conv_euro (the verifier's baseline). Also reported against conv_euro_t; a failure against conv_euro_t is reported as 'does not beat a tuned filter'.
pass_rules.P3_aim_error: in both datasets: aim error difference upper bound <= +0.005 against conv_euro and against the tracker row.
pass_rules.P4_lag: in both datasets: along_det (point) in the > 0.1 bin >= tracker - 0.02 and >= conv_euro - 0.02; in the 0.03-0.1 bin >= tracker - 0.015 and >= conv_euro - 0.015; and TMOT >= 100 px, > 0.1 bin, along_raw >= -0.05 (round 1: -0.099, tracker -0.023).
pass_rules.P5_first_rows: in both datasets where at least 20 new small-person states exist: first5 mean dh (people under 100 px) <= conv_euro + 0.010 and share of row-1 steps > 0.15 <= 0.05 (round 1 TMOT: 79 %).
pass_rules.verdict: v2 PASSES only if P1-P5 all hold for the same candidate. Anything else is reported as a failure of the named rule, with the numbers.

device_rate: no GT. Recordings already processed by the size-mode workflow on this PC (read only): v2/data/det and v2/data/gmc for rec_person1 (MEASURE_20261109_140236_2, 1446 frames) and the two rec_inside recordings (MEASURE_20261110_165240, 287; MEASURE_20261110_170437, 107), 23-24 fps, both detectors. Tracker rows = server ByteTrack as scripts/track_run.py (imported, not written). Reported, not part of the pass rules: dh p95 / p99, per-track largest dh, aim step p99, aim jitter (reference height = tracker row height), lag against the detection along the detection's own 3-frame motion per speed bin, first-5-rows steps; for tracker, euro, conv_euro, gru_v1, gru_v2, gru_v2_size.
cost: PC, one thread, the numpy engine + GRU + size filter for 10 / 20 / 30 people per frame (median ms per frame over 300 frames, best of 3).
not_done_here: no server code change, no device run, no push. gru_v2/SERVER_NOTES.md describes what the server must compute; weights exported as npz + json like round 1.

amendment_1.written: 2026-11-15 21:17, while the 8 training runs were still running and before any val-A or val-B metric of any method was computed by gru_v2 code
amendment_1.change: selection_valA.score: the first5 ratio is (first5 mean dh + 0.02) / (conv_euro first5 mean dh + 0.02) instead of the plain ratio. Reason: the verifier measured conv_euro's first-row steps at about 0.007 heights; a plain ratio against such a small number would let this one term decide J. 0.02 heights is a step too small to matter on screen. Nothing else changes.
